AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Ventriculo-peritoneal (VP) shunt is the most frequent treatment for hydrocephalus. Its malfunctioning represents one of the most common problem in neurosurgical practice, often requiring shunt revision procedures. In some cases, the complete removal of a VP shunt may present difficulties, leading the surgeon to leave the ventricular catheter in situ. This decision is often taken in order to avoid possible adverse events, first of all, life-threatening hemorrhagic risks. However, a non-functioning catheter left in the ventricular system represents a prosthetic device which may lead to further complications.

AbstractText.Label: CASE DESCRIPTION
AbstractText.content: We report on the case of an adult man presenting a tumor-like cystic lesion, with mural and nodular post-contrast enhancement, caused by a huge granuloma formed around the tip of a retained ventricular catheter.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: This occurrence is extremely rare and it is the first reported case in the literature. Preoperative diagnosis was challenging and included infection, metastasis, dysembriogenetic lesions and the rare reversible poroencephalic cysts. The development of the granuloma may have been the result of persistent chronic inflammatory reactions between the ventricular catheter left in situ and the brain parenchyma, according to several physiopathogenetic theories recently reported in the literature. Application of neuroendoscopic techniques are improving the management of VP shunt revisions, allowing a safe removal of the catheters stuck or lost in the ventricular system. Thus, they may represent an additional option to avoid the possible complications related to retained ventricular catheters.
